Plaintiff Brendan Ngwa Nforbi ("Plaintiff") alleges as follows against Defendant Diamond
Truck Sales, Inc. ("Diamond" or "Defendant") and Does | through 20:
Plaintiff BRENDAN NGWA NFORBI ("Plaintiff") is an individual residing in Stockton,
California, San Joaquin County.
Defendant DIAMOND TRUCK SALES, INC. ("Diamond") is a California corporation
engaged in the business of selling commercial trucks, with locations including 480 Peachoid Road,
Gaffney, South Carolina 29341; 1201 South Soderquist Road, Turlock, California 95380; 7156
Page 1
COMPLAINT FOR FRAUD, BREACH OF CONTRACT, AND RELATED CLAIMS

Goldenstate Highway, Bakersfield, California 93308; and 5201 Bridge Street, Fort Worth, Texas
The true names and capacities of Defendants sued as DOES 1 through 20 are unknown to
Plaintiff, who therefore sues said Defendants by fictitious names. Plaintiff will amend this
Complaint to show the true names and capacities when ascertained. Plaintiff is informed and
believes, and on that basis alleges, that each fictitiously named Defendant is legally responsible for
the events and damages described herein.
II]. JURISDICTION AND VENUE
This Court has jurisdiction pursuant to Code of Civil Procedure section 410.10. The amount
in controversy exceeds $25,000, exclusive of interest and costs.
Venue is proper in San Joaquin County because Plaintiff resides in this County, the Truck
was garaged and intended for operation here, Plaintiff's injuries were suffered here, and Defendant
conducts business in California giving rise to the claims alleged herein.
II. INTRODUCTION
This action arises from Defendant's sale of a commercial diesel semi-truck that was not fit for
lawful operation in California and suffered from material, undisclosed emissions defects at the time
of sale.
Defendant knowingly sold a vehicle into California commerce that had been previously
rendered inoperable by a California enforcement agency due to emissions and/or safety non-
compliance, and concealed these material facts from Plaintiff to induce his purchase.
On or about April 4, 2023, Plaintiff purchased a 2014 Volvo VNL diesel semi-truck, VIN
4V4NC9EHGEN 142206 (the "Truck"), from Diamond for use in commercial freight operations
based in California. The purchase price was $26,900.00, with total charges of $27,092.75. At the
time of sale, Diamond failed to disclose that the Truck suffered from a severe Diesel Exhaust Fluid
Page 2
COMPLAINT FOR FRAUD, BREACH OF CONTRACT, AND RELATED CLAIMS

("DEF") and emissions system defect affecting the selective catalytic reduction ("SCR") system,
which rendered the Truck non-compliant with California emissions regulations and unsafe for
highway operation.
On information and belief, the prior owner of the Truck expressly disclosed this DEF/
emissions defect to Diamond before Diamond resold the Truck to Plaintiff. Plaintiff is informed and
believes that prior to Plaintiff's purchase, the prior owner provided Diamond with written and/or
verbal notice of the DEF system failure and engine derate condition. Discovery is expected to
confirm this. Despite this actual knowledge, Diamond sold the Truck to Plaintiff without disclosing
its non-compliant condition.
On information and belief, at or around the time Diamond acquired the Truck and/or
Plaintiff's purchase, a California enforcement agency had cited or placed an out-of-service order on
the Truck for emissions or safety violations. Plaintiff is investigating the precise nature of this
designation and will amend once confirmed. This regulatory determination was not disclosed to
Plaintiff.
Shortly after purchase, while Plaintiff was operating the Truck on a commercial route under a
Lease-On Owner Operator Agreement, the Truck experienced a catastrophic emissions failure,
entered engine derate ("limp mode"), emitted excessive black smoke, and became incapable of
exceeding approximately 35 miles per hour, rendering it commercially unusable and unsafe for
highway operation.
Plaintiff incurred substantial economic losses, including purchase funds and down payment
exceeding $12,000, regulatory and registration fees exceeding $3,400, financing-related charges
and payments, towing and attempted repair costs, storage and insurance expenses, and lost business
opportunities and freight income.
Page 3
COMPLAINT FOR FRAUD, BREACH OF CONTRACT, AND RELATED CLAIMS

IV. FACTUAL ALLEGATIONS
A. The Purchase Transaction
On or about April 4, 2023, Plaintiff purchased the Truck from Diamond for a cash price of
$26,900.00, with total charges of $27,092.75, as reflected in the Retail Buyer's Order executed at
that time.
Plaintiff paid a down payment exceeding $12,000 to Diamond, with the remaining balance
financed through a third-party lender selected, arranged, or facilitated by Diamond in connection
with the Truck's sale.
Diamond knew or reasonably should have known that the Truck was being purchased for
commercial operation involving California, where emissions compliance is mandatory for lawful
operation of heavy-duty diesel vehicles.
As part of the transaction, Plaintiff executed a Power of Attorney authorizing Diamond and
its employees to act on Plaintiff's behalf with the California Department of Motor Vehicles for
purposes of titling and registration of the Truck. This document was notarized in San Joaquin
County, California.
B. Undisclosed Emissions Defect and Regulatory Non-Compliance
At the time of sale, the Truck suffered from a serious DEF/emissions system defect affecting
the SCR system, resulting in excessive emissions, engine derate, loss of power, and entry into limp
mode.
This defect rendered the Truck non-compliant with California emissions requirements for
heavy-duty diesel vehicles, including regulations enforced by the California Air Resources Board
and California Code of Regulations, title 13, section 2025 (Truck and Bus Regulation), preventing
its lawful registration and operation in the state.
On information and belief, the emissions defect existed prior to Plaintiff's purchase and was
Page 4
COMPLAINT FOR FRAUD, BREACH OF CONTRACT, AND RELATED CLAIMS

known or should have been known to Diamond before resale. Plaintiff is informed and believes that
prior to Plaintiff's purchase, the prior owner provided Diamond with written and/or verbal notice of
the DEF system failure and engine derate condition. Discovery is expected to confirm this.
On information and belief, at or around the time Diamond acquired the Truck and/or
Plaintiff's purchase, a California enforcement agency had cited or placed an out-of-service order on
the Truck for emissions or safety violations. Plaintiff is investigating the precise nature of this
designation and will amend once confirmed. This regulatory determination provided Diamond with
notice of the Truck's unlawful condition.
Diamond did not disclose the emissions defect, the Truck's regulatory non-compliance, the
prior owner's disclosures, or any enforcement agency inoperable or out-of-service designation to
Plaintiff. The emissions defect and enforcement designation were facts exclusively within
Diamond's knowledge and not ascertainable by Plaintiff through reasonable inspection or publicly
available records at the time of sale.
A heavy-duty diesel vehicle that cannot meet California emissions requirements cannot
lawfully operate in this state. Defendant had a statutory duty under California Vehicle Code section
24007 not to sell a vehicle that does not comply with the Health and Safety Code provisions
regarding emissions. This statutory duty overrides any contractual "As-Is" disclaimers. Plaintiff
would not have purchased the Truck had the true facts been disclosed.
C. Mechanical Failure and Resulting Harm
Shortly after purchase, while operating the Truck on a commercial route under Plaintiff's
Lease-On Owner Operator Agreement, the Truck experienced a severe emissions failure.
The Truck entered limp mode, emitted black smoke, and became incapable of safe highway
operation, being unable to exceed approximately 35 miles per hour. This failure pattern is consistent
with the DEF/SCR/emissions system defect described above.
Page 5
COMPLAINT FOR FRAUD, BREACH OF CONTRACT, AND RELATED CLAIMS

The Truck was rendered commercially unusable and unsafe, resulting in immediate and
continuing economic losses to Plaintiff. Due to the immediate financial losses and capital depletion
caused by Defendant's conduct, Plaintiff was unable to procure a replacement commercial vehicle.
Plaintiff's documented economic losses include, without limitation:
(a) A $12,345.10 deposit paid under the Retail Buyer's Order;
(b) A $1,895.00 GAP enrollment charge under the GAP addendum;
(c) DMV and registration fees totaling $3,442.00 as reflected in the DMV receipt;
(d) Towing and repair costs, including $1,197.34 paid to Brannon Tire, $450.00 paid to
Golden Empire Towing, $800.00 paid to Mobile Will's Repair, and $5,000.00 paid
to Almaraz Diesel Repairs;
({e) Additional storage, insurance, and related expenses associated with the Truck.
The subtotal of Plaintiff's documented direct economic losses from the deposit, GAP enrollment,
DMV fees, and the above repair and towing charges is approximately $25,129.44, exclusive of lost
income and interest.
At the time of purchase, Plaintiff had secured or was actively pursuing hauling contracts,
including through Amazon Relay, and reasonably projected net weekly earnings of approximately
$1,800. Due to the Truck's failure, Plaintiff was unable to perform under those arrangements and
lost that income. Plaintiff has suffered lost net commercial income of not less than $46,800 to date,
with continuing losses according to proof.
Plaintiff was unable to mitigate these losses by renting or purchasing a replacement vehicle
because his available capital was exhausted by the down payment and repair costs for the subject
Truck.
Page 6
COMPLAINT FOR FRAUD, BREACH OF CONTRACT, AND RELATED CLAIMS

V. CAUSES OF ACTION
FIRST CAUSE OF ACTION
(Fraudulent Concealment Against All Defendants)
Plaintiff re-alleges and incorporates by reference each and every paragraph above as though
fully set forth herein.
Diamond concealed and failed to disclose material facts regarding the Truck's emissions
defect and regulatory non-compliance, including the prior owner's disclosure of DEF/emissions
issues and the enforcement agency inoperable or out-of-service determination.
Diamond had actual and superior knowledge of these facts and a duty to disclose them to
Plaintiff before inducing his purchase of the Truck. The emissions defect and regulatory non-
compliance were not reasonably discoverable by Plaintiff through ordinary inspection at the time of
sale. Diamond possessed superior knowledge of facts not accessible to Plaintiff through reasonable
inspection or publicly available records. (See Warner Constr. Corp. v. City of Los Angeles (1970) 2
Cal.3d 285 [duty to disclose in sales transactions]; Civ. Code, § 1710.)
Diamond intentionally concealed these facts with the intent to induce Plaintiff to purchase
the Truck and to pay funds in reliance on the belief that it was lawful and fit for commercial
operation in California.
Plaintiff reasonably relied on Diamond's concealment and would not have purchased the
Truck, or would have paid substantially less and on different terms, had the true facts been
disclosed.
As a direct and proximate result of Diamond's fraudulent concealment, Plaintiff suffered
damages according to proof at trial.
The names of the specific agents of Diamond who participated in the concealment are known
to Defendant but unknown to Plaintiff at this time. Plaintiff is informed and believes, and thereon
Page 7
COMPLAINT FOR FRAUD, BREACH OF CONTRACT, AND RELATED CLAIMS

alleges, that Diamond's agents, including the salesperson and/or finance manager who facilitated
the April 4, 2023 transaction, acted within the course and scope of their employment in concealing
the material facts described herein.
Defendant's conduct was intentional, malicious, and oppressive, done with a willful and
conscious disregard of Plaintiff's nghts, justifying an award of punitive and exemplary damages
pursuant to Civil Code section 3294. |
SECOND CAUSE OF ACTION
(Intentional Misrepresentation Against All Defendants)
Plaintiff re-alleges and incorporates by reference each and every paragraph above as though
fully set forth herein.
Diamond represented, expressly and by omission, that the Truck was fit for commercial
operation and lawful for use in California.
These representations were false and were known by Diamond to be false at the time they
were made, because Diamond knew of the DEF/emissions defect, the Truck's non-compliance with
California emissions regulations, and the enforcement agency inoperable or out-of-service
determination.
Diamond intended that Plaintiff rely on these representations in deciding to purchase the
Truck.
Plaintiff reasonably relied on Diamond's representations and, as a direct and proximate result,
suffered damages in an amount to be proven at trial.
Defendant's conduct was intentional, malicious, and oppressive, done with a willful and
conscious disregard of Plaintiff's rights, justifying an award of punitive and exemplary damages
pursuant to Civil Code section 3294,
Page 8
COMPLAINT FOR FRAUD, BREACH OF CONTRACT, AND RELATED CLAIMS

THIRD CAUSE OF ACTION
(Negligent Misrepresentation Against All Defendants)
Plaintiff re-alleges and incorporates by reference each and every paragraph above as though
fully set forth herein.
In the alternative, Diamond made representations regarding the Truck's condition, emissions
compliance, and fitness for commercial use without reasonable grounds for believing them to be
true.
Diamond owed Plaintiff a duty to exercise reasonable care in making representations
concerning the Truck's condition and regulatory status. (See Bily v. Arthur Young & Co. (1992)
3 Cal.4th 370.)
Plaintiff reasonably relied on Diamond's representations to his detriment and suffered
damages as a result.
FOURTH CAUSE OF ACTION
(Breach of Contract Against Defendant Diamond)
Plaintiff re-alleges and incorporates by reference each and every paragraph above as though
fully set forth herein.
Plaintiff and Diamond entered into a written purchase agreement and related sales documents
for the Truck, including the Retail Buyer's Order executed on or about April 4, 2023, reflecting a
purchase price of $26,900.00, VIN 4V4NC9EH6EN 142206, and total charges of $27,092.75.
Diamond breached the contract by delivering a vehicle that was not fit for its ordinary
commercial purpose and could not lawfully be operated in California, contrary to the implied and
reasonably understood terms of the parties' agreement.
Plaintiff performed all conditions required of him under the agreement, including payment
of the down payment and execution of necessary paperwork, or his performance was excused.
Page 9
COMPLAINT FOR FRAUD, BREACH OF CONTRACT, AND RELATED CLAIMS

As a direct and proximate result of Diamond's breach, Plaintiff suffered damages in an
amount to be proven at trial.
Plaintiff is entitled to prejudgment interest on his liquidated economic losses at the legal rate from
the date of loss pursuant to Civil Code section 3287, subdivision (a).
FIFTH CAUSE OF ACTION
(Violation of Unfair Competition Law, Bus. & Prof. Code § 17200 Against All Defendants)
Plaintiff re-alleges and incorporates by reference each and every paragraph above as though
fully set forth herein.
Diamond engaged in unlawful, unfair, and fraudulent business practices by selling a non-
compliant commercial vehicle into California commerce while concealing its emissions defect,
regulatory non-compliance, and prior enforcement agency inoperable or out-of-service status.
Diamond's conduct was unlawful in that it violated California emissions regulations,
including California Code of Regulations, title 13, section 2020 (emissions compliance
requirements), California Vehicle Code section 24007 (dealer duty to ensure vehicle meets
emissions standards at sale), and Health and Safety Code section 43000 et seq. (motor vehicle
emissions standards), and constituted fraud and deceit under California law. Selling a vehicle
with a non-functional emissions system violates federal and state environmenta! laws, including the
Federal Clean Air Act, making Diamond's business practice unlawful per se.
Diamond's conduct was unfair because it caused substantial injury to Plaintiff that he could
not reasonably avoid and that is not outweighed by any countervailing benefits to consumers or
competition. (See Cel-Tech Communications, Inc. v. Los Angeles Cellular Telephone Co. (1999) 20
Cal.4th 163.)
Diamond's conduct was fraudulent because it was likely to deceive reasonable consumers,
including Plaintiff, into believing they were purchasing a truck that could lawfully operate in
Page 10
COMPLAINT FOR FRAUD, BREACH OF CONTRACT, AND RELATED CLAIMS

California.
As aresult of Diamond's violations of Business and Professions Code section 17200 et seq.,
Plaintiff suffered economic injury and seeks restitution, disgorgement, injunctive relief, and all
other relief permitted by statute.
SIXTH CAUSE OF ACTION
(Rescission and Restitution Against Defendant Diamond)
Plaintiff re-alleges and incorporates by reference each and every paragraph above as though
fully set forth herein.
Diamond's fraud, concealment, and misrepresentations entitle Plaintiff to rescind the Truck
purchase transaction pursuant to Civil Code section 1689, subdivision (b)(1) (fraud) and
subdivision (b)(5) (failure of consideration).
Plaintiff seeks restitution of all monies paid in connection with the transaction, including but
not limited to the down payment, financed amounts paid to date, registration and DMV fees,
exemption-related expenses, towing and repair costs, storage and insurance, and other out-of-pocket
costs.
Money damages alone cannot fully restore the parties to their pre-contract positions or
unwind the transaction, and Plaintiff therefore seeks rescission together with restitution of all
amounts paid.
SEVENTH CAUSE OF ACTION
(Declaratory Relief Against All Defendants)
Plaintiff re-alleges and incorporates by reference each and every paragraph above as though
fully set forth herein.
An actual controversy exists between Plaintiff and Diamond concerning their respective
rights and obligations arising from the Truck purchase transaction. (Code Civ. Proc., § 1060.)
Page 11
COMPLAINT FOR FRAUD, BREACH OF CONTRACT, AND RELATED CLAIMS

Plaintiff contends that the purchase agreement is voidable and unenforceable due to
Diamond's fraudulent conduct and material non-disclosures, and that Plaintiff is entitled to rescind
the transaction and recover all consideration paid. Diamond disputes, or is expected to dispute,
these contentions.
In the alternative, and to the extent this cause of action is duplicative of the Sixth Cause of
Action for Rescission and Restitution, Plaintiff pleads this cause of action as an alternative form of
relief. Plaintiff seeks a judicial declaration that the purchase agreement is voidable, that Plaintiff is
entitled to rescind the transaction, and that Diamond must return all consideration paid in
connection with the Truck's purchase.
VI. PRAYER FOR RELIEF
WHEREFORE, Plaintiff prays for judgment against Defendant Diamond Truck Sales, Inc. and
Does | through 20 as follows:
A. For rescission of the vehicle purchase transaction;
B. For restitution of all monies paid, including down payment, financed amounts paid to date,
registration and DMV fees, exemption-related fees, and related costs;
C. For compensatory damages according to proof at trial;
D. For consequential damages, including lost business income and opportunities;
E. For punitive and exemplary damages according to proof pursuant to Civil Code section 3294;
F, For disgorgement and restitution under the Unfair Competition Law;
G. For costs of suit incurred herein;
H. For prejudgment interest on liquidated damages from the date of Plaintiff's out-of-pocket
expenditures pursuant to Civil Code section 3287, subdivision (a), and post-judgment interest as
permitted by law;
I. For such other and further relicf as the Court deems just and proper.

Plaintiff demands a trial by jury on all issues so triable.

VIII.  PREJUDGMENT INTEREST
26. The documented out-of-pocket losses set forth in Section IV are liquidated and certain,
or capable of being made certain by calculation, and the right to recover them vested on the dates
each charge was incurred. I am therefore entitled to prejudgment interest on those amounts at the
legal rate of seven percent (7%) per annum (Cal. Const., art. XV, section 1) from the date of loss
to the date of judgment, pursuant to Civil Code section 3287, subdivision (a). (See North Oakland
Medical Clinic v. Rogers (1998) 65 Cal.App.4th 824, 828-830.)
27. For purposes of this prove-up I have computed prejudgment interest using a single,
conservative weighted-average start date of June 1, 2023 (the approximate midpoint of the dates
on which the documented charges in Section IV were incurred, from April 4, 2023 through June
23, 2023), applied to the $20,218.65 documented out-of-pocket subtotal through June 15, 2026:
$20,218.65 x 7% x approximately 3.04 years (06/01/2023 to 06/15/2026) = $4,302.55. I treat that
$4,302.55 figure as a conservative fixed amount through June 15, 2026 and do not seek additional
prejudgment interest for the period after that date in this request.
28. I have not sought prejudgment interest on the lost-income component in Section VI,
because lost income is not liquidated within the meaning of Civil Code section 3287, subdivision
(a).

7f, Plaintiff waives costs and disbursements in connection with this request for court judgment.

the DEF/SCR system. I paid approximately $5,000.00 for that work. I did not receive an
itemized written receipt.
17. The two undocumented amounts above total $5,750.00. I respectfully request that the
Court consider them on the basis of my sworn testimony, in light of the corroborating
documentary evidence -- specifically, the contemporaneous CVC section 22852 Notice (Exh. 10)
and the Golden Empire Towing invoice (Exh. 8), which together establish the chain of custody
between the storage release and Almaraz Diesel. To the extent the Court declines to award the
undocumented amounts, my documented out-of-pocket subtotal of $20,218.65 (Section IV above)
is fully supported by Exhibits 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 8, and 9.
VI.  LOST COMMERCIAL INCOME
18. Because of the truck's failure I was unable to perform under the Lease-On Owner
Operator Agreement with Gobbato Builders, LLC (Exh. 4), and I was unable to dispatch any
meaningful number of loads through the Amazon Relay platform (Exh. 5). The truck was
operational for only a matter of days before catastrophic failure. By late May 2023 it had been
towed and stored under Vehicle Code section 22852. By June 23, 2023 the final attempted repair
(the Western Truck Center lamp work, Exh. 9) had failed to restore commercial operability. The
truck was thereafter rendered permanently commercially unusable.

was set up to operate at a 10% lease-on fee -- meaning I would have netted approximately 90% of
gross load revenue, less fuel, insurance, and incidental expenses. Based on prevailing rates on the
Amazon Relay platform in 2023 and my reasonable expectations at the time the FAC was filed, I
had projected and pleaded approximately $1,800 in net weekly earnings had the truck been
operational. (FAC, paragraph 31.)
20. For purposes of this prove-up, and recognizing that I do not have month-by-month
settlement statements documenting every load I would have hauled, I respectfully request lost
commercial income on a deliberately conservative basis: 18 weeks of lost operation (conservative
-- May through September 2023) at $1,300/week (well below the $1,800 pleaded in FAC
paragraph 31), for a subtotal of $23,400.00.
21. The $23,400.00 figure is approximately one half of the lower bound of lost income I
pleaded in the FAC at paragraph 31, which alleged "lost net commercial income of not less than
approximately $46,800 to date, with continuing losses according to proof at trial." I have
deliberately requested only a conservative fraction of the lost income I sustained, in recognition
of the prove-up evidentiary posture and the absence of weekly settlement statements in my
possession.
VII.  RESCISSION, RESTITUTION, AND DECLARATORY RELIEF

1691 and 1693. The truck has been irrecoverably damaged by the underlying defect and the
storage process. Restoration of the truck to its original condition is impossible and is therefore
excused under Civil Code section 1693, and this Court is authorized to adjust the equities
between the parties under that statute.

VIII.  PREJUDGMENT INTEREST
26. The documented out-of-pocket losses set forth in Section IV are liquidated and certain,
or capable of being made certain by calculation, and the right to recover them vested on the dates
each charge was incurred. I am therefore entitled to prejudgment interest on those amounts at the
legal rate of seven percent (7%) per annum (Cal. Const., art. XV, section 1) from the date of loss
to the date of judgment, pursuant to Civil Code section 3287, subdivision (a). (See North Oakland
Medical Clinic v. Rogers (1998) 65 Cal.App.4th 824, 828-830.)
27. For purposes of this prove-up I have computed prejudgment interest using a single,
conservative weighted-average start date of June 1, 2023 (the approximate midpoint of the dates
on which the documented charges in Section IV were incurred, from April 4, 2023 through June
23, 2023), applied to the $20,218.65 documented out-of-pocket subtotal through June 15, 2026:
$20,218.65 x 7% x approximately 3.04 years (06/01/2023 to 06/15/2026) = $4,302.55. I treat that
$4,302.55 figure as a conservative fixed amount through June 15, 2026 and do not seek additional
prejudgment interest for the period after that date in this request.
28. I have not sought prejudgment interest on the lost-income component in Section VI,
because lost income is not liquidated within the meaning of Civil Code section 3287, subdivision
(a).

I.  PRELIMINARY STATEMENT

matters set forth herein are within my personal knowledge unless stated on information and

2. This Declaration is submitted together with the following companion documents
constituting my prove-up package: (a) Plaintiff's Request for Entry of Default Judgment (Form
CIV-100), including the Declaration of Nonmilitary Status at CIV-100 item 8; (b) Plaintiff's
[Proposed] Judgment by Court After Default (Form JUD-100); and (c) the documentary exhibits
referenced herein and listed in the Index of Exhibits below. Plaintiff waives costs of suit on
CIV-100 item 7f; no Memorandum of Costs (Form MC-010) is filed with this packet.
II.  PROCEDURAL POSTURE
3. The operative pleading in this action is the First Amended Complaint ("FAC"), which
asserts eight causes of action against Defendant Diamond: (1) Fraudulent Concealment; (2)
Intentional Misrepresentation; (3) Negligent Misrepresentation; (4) Breach of Contract; (5)
Breach of Implied Warranty of Merchantability (Cal. Comm. Code section 2314); (6) Violation of
the Unfair Competition Law (Bus. & Prof. Code section 17200 et seq.); (7) Rescission and
Restitution; and (8) Declaratory Relief.
4. The FAC was personally served on Diamond on May 12, 2026, and the Proof of
Service was filed with this Court on May 18, 2026. Diamond's deadline to respond to the FAC
expired on June 11, 2026. Diamond filed no responsive pleading, demurrer, or other appearance. I
have submitted a Request for Entry of Default (Form CIV-100) against Diamond, and the Court
has entered, or will shortly enter, Diamond's default as reflected in the Court's file.
5. Because Diamond has defaulted, the well-pleaded factual allegations of the FAC
concerning liability are deemed admitted. (Steven M. Garber & Assocs. v. Eskandarian (2007)
150 Cal.App.4th 813, 823; Kim v. Westmoore Partners, Inc. (2011) 201 Cal.App.4th 267, 281.)
The well-pleaded allegations include, without limitation: that Diamond knowingly sold to me a
2014 Volvo VNL diesel semi-truck (VIN 4V4NC9EH6EN142206) that suffered from an
undisclosed and material defect in its Diesel Exhaust Fluid ("DEF") and Selective Catalytic
Reduction ("SCR") emissions systems; that the defect rendered the truck non-compliant with
California emissions law and unsafe for highway operation; that Diamond had pre-sale

knowledge of the defect and concealed it; and that Diamond's conduct was intentional, malicious,
fraudulent, and oppressive within the meaning of Civil Code section 3294.
6. This Declaration addresses only the amount and proof of damages. I have made no
effort to relitigate liability, which is deemed established by the default.
III.  THE TRANSACTION AND THE FAILURE
7. On April 4, 2023, I purchased the subject truck (2014 Volvo VNL, VIN
4V4NC9EH6EN142206) from Diamond. The transaction was documented by a Retail Buyer's
Order reflecting a Cash Price of $26,900.00 and Total Charges of $27,092.75 after document and
title fees. A true and correct copy of the Retail Buyer's Order is attached as Exhibit 1.
8. I paid Diamond a deposit of $12,345.10 by certified funds at the time of sale. This
amount appears in the "DEPOSIT" line and is reflected in the "TOTAL CREDITS" line of the
Retail Buyer's Order (Exh. 1, p. 1).
9. The remaining balance of $14,747.65 was financed through a third-party lender, Dakota
Financial LLC, which was selected, arranged, or facilitated by Diamond in connection with the
sale.
10. In connection with titling the truck I was billed by the California Department of Motor
Vehicles in the amount of $3,442.00 for use tax, weight, transfer, and related fees required to
complete registration. The California DMV "Generated Fees" printout dated May 8, 2023 reflects
Total Fees Due of $3,442.00. I have not yet paid this amount because the truck failed before
registration could be completed, leaving me with an outstanding DMV obligation that continues
to accrue penalties. The California DMV "Generated Fees" printout and the corresponding DMV
Report of Deposit of Fees and Application materials are attached as Exhibit 2. I include this
amount in my damages because it is a real, documented financial obligation owed to the State of
California as a direct consequence of Diamond's sale to me of a defective and non-compliant
truck.
11. In connection with the sale Diamond also enrolled me in a GAP product, for which I
was charged $1,895.00 under a separate GAP Addendum. A true and correct copy of the GAP
Addendum is attached as Exhibit 3.

12. I purchased the truck specifically to use it in commercial freight service under my own
owner-operator authority. On April 27, 2023, twenty-three days after purchase, I executed a
Lease-On Owner Operator Agreement with Gobbato Builders, LLC (MC #1357325) under which
I would haul freight for compensation paid weekly by Friday settlement. The Lease-On
Agreement specifically identifies my truck by VIN. A true and correct copy of the Lease-On
Owner Operator Agreement is attached as Exhibit 4. On the same day, April 27, 2023, my
Amazon Relay driver account was activated, providing me with access to dispatch hauling loads
through the Amazon Relay platform. A true and correct copy of the Amazon Relay driver setup
verification, bearing my signature and the platform's digital verification code of April 27, 2023
9:22 AM PDT, is attached as Exhibit 5.
13. Within days of beginning operations the truck experienced exactly the failure mode
characteristic of the DEF/SCR defect alleged in the FAC: it entered engine derate ("limp mode"),
emitted excessive black smoke, lost power, and became incapable of exceeding approximately 35
miles per hour. The truck was thereby rendered commercially unusable and unsafe for highway
operation. Despite my repeated attempts to repair it (described in Sections IV and V below), the
truck never returned to lawful commercial service.

contemporaneous record of the corresponding charge or obligation. None of these losses would
have been incurred but for Diamond's sale to me of the defective and non-compliant truck. With
respect to item (c), the $3,442.00 DMV obligation is fully documented by Exhibit 2, remains
outstanding, and continues to accrue penalties -- making it an ongoing and expanding
consequence of the transaction.
V.  ADDITIONAL OUT-OF-POCKET LOSSES -- NO CONTEMPORANEOUS RECEIPT
16. In addition to the documented charges set forth above, I personally paid in cash, from
my own funds, two further amounts for emergency services performed on the truck. Although I
did not retain itemized written receipts -- despite having requested them at the time -- these
payments are facts within my direct personal knowledge, and the surrounding contemporaneous
record corroborates that the truck was in storage, released, transported, and delivered for repair
during this period:
(a) Commercial Towing storage-release fee -- $750.00. On or about May 23, 2023, the truck
was towed and stored under California Vehicle Code section 22852 by Commercial Towing,
located at 2609 Texas Street, Bakersfield, California. The contemporaneous Notice of Stored
Vehicle issued under Vehicle Code section 22852 is attached as Exhibit 10. I paid Commercial
Towing $750.00 in cash to release the truck. I requested a written receipt but the operator did not
provide one.
(b) Almaraz Diesel repair -- $5,000.00. After the truck was released from Commercial
Towing, Golden Empire Towing transported it (under the invoice constituting Exh. 8) to Almaraz
Diesel, which at that time was operating out of Diamond's Bakersfield, California location.
Almaraz Diesel performed diagnostic and repair work on the DEF/SCR system. I paid
approximately $5,000.00 for that work. I did not receive an itemized written receipt.
17. The two undocumented amounts above total $5,750.00. I respectfully request that the
Court consider them on the basis of my sworn testimony, in light of the corroborating

VI.  LOST COMMERCIAL INCOME
18. Because of the truck's failure I was unable to perform under the Lease-On Owner
Operator Agreement with Gobbato Builders, LLC (Exh. 4), and I was unable to dispatch any
meaningful number of loads through the Amazon Relay platform (Exh. 5). The truck was
operational for only a matter of days before catastrophic failure. By late May 2023 it had been
towed and stored under Vehicle Code section 22852. By June 23, 2023 the final attempted repair
(the Western Truck Center lamp work, Exh. 9) had failed to restore commercial operability. The
truck was thereafter rendered permanently commercially unusable.
19. Under the Lease-On Agreement with Gobbato Builders, LLC (Exh. 4, paragraph III), I
was set up to operate at a 10% lease-on fee -- meaning I would have netted approximately 90% of
gross load revenue, less fuel, insurance, and incidental expenses. Based on prevailing rates on the
Amazon Relay platform in 2023 and my reasonable expectations at the time the FAC was filed, I
had projected and pleaded approximately $1,800 in net weekly earnings had the truck been
operational. (FAC, paragraph 31.)
20. For purposes of this prove-up, and recognizing that I do not have month-by-month
settlement statements documenting every load I would have hauled, I respectfully request lost
commercial income on a deliberately conservative basis: 18 weeks of lost operation (conservative
-- May through September 2023) at $1,300/week (well below the $1,800 pleaded in FAC
paragraph 31), for a subtotal of $23,400.00.
21. The $23,400.00 figure is approximately one half of the lower bound of lost income I
pleaded in the FAC at paragraph 31, which alleged "lost net commercial income of not less than
approximately $46,800 to date, with continuing losses according to proof at trial." I have
deliberately requested only a conservative fraction of the lost income I sustained, in recognition

VII.  RESCISSION, RESTITUTION, AND DECLARATORY RELIEF
22. I gave notice of rescission within the FAC itself, as permitted by Civil Code sections
1691 and 1693. The truck has been irrecoverably damaged by the underlying defect and the
storage process. Restoration of the truck to its original condition is impossible and is therefore
excused under Civil Code section 1693, and this Court is authorized to adjust the equities
between the parties under that statute.
23. The $14,747.65 financed balance was originated through Dakota Financial LLC,
which is not a party to this action. I do not seek in this Declaration a money judgment in the
amount of the financed balance itself, because that obligation is between me and a non-party
lender and recovering it from Diamond would risk a double recovery if I later resolve the
financing separately.
24. I reserve the right, after entry of judgment, to seek a separate determination of any
indemnification or further restitution remedy as to the financed balance if and as appropriate
under Civil Code section 1693 and the Court's continuing equitable jurisdiction over the
rescission count.
25. Specific Judgment Findings Requested. In addition to the monetary relief itemized in
Sections IV through VIII of this Declaration, I respectfully request that the Court's Judgment
include the following findings and declarations. Each falls squarely within the scope of the FAC's
Seventh Cause of Action (Rescission and Restitution) and Eighth Cause of Action (Declaratory
Relief), and each is supported by well-pleaded allegations of the FAC that are deemed admitted
by Diamond's default: (a) That the April 4, 2023 purchase transaction between Plaintiff and
Diamond Truck Sales, Inc. -- including the Retail Buyer's Order (Exh. 1) and the GAP Addendum
(Exh. 3) -- is rescinded pursuant to Civil Code section 1689, subdivision (b), and is of no further
force or effect as between Plaintiff and Diamond, so that Diamond may not enforce any term of,
or claim any continuing benefit under, that transaction. (b) That Diamond's conduct in connection
with the sale of the subject truck constituted unlawful, unfair, and fraudulent business acts and

VIII.  PREJUDGMENT INTEREST
26. The documented out-of-pocket losses set forth in Section IV are liquidated and certain,
or capable of being made certain by calculation, and the right to recover them vested on the dates
each charge was incurred. I am therefore entitled to prejudgment interest on those amounts at the
legal rate of seven percent (7%) per annum (Cal. Const., art. XV, section 1) from the date of loss
to the date of judgment, pursuant to Civil Code section 3287, subdivision (a). (See North Oakland
Medical Clinic v. Rogers (1998) 65 Cal.App.4th 824, 828-830.)
27. For purposes of this prove-up I have computed prejudgment interest using a single,
conservative weighted-average start date of June 1, 2023 (the approximate midpoint of the dates
on which the documented charges in Section IV were incurred, from April 4, 2023 through June
23, 2023), applied to the $20,218.65 documented out-of-pocket subtotal through June 15, 2026:
$20,218.65 x 7% x approximately 3.04 years (06/01/2023 to 06/15/2026) = $4,302.55. I treat that
$4,302.55 figure as a conservative fixed amount through June 15, 2026 and do not seek additional
prejudgment interest for the period after that date in this request.
28. I have not sought prejudgment interest on the lost-income component in Section VI,
because lost income is not liquidated within the meaning of Civil Code section 3287, subdivision
(a).
IX.  PUNITIVE DAMAGES
29. The FAC pleads, and Diamond's default admits, that Diamond's conduct was
intentional, malicious, fraudulent, and oppressive within the meaning of Civil Code section 3294.
(FAC, paragraph 47.) Punitive damages are accordingly available on the First Cause of Action
(Fraudulent Concealment) and the Second Cause of Action (Intentional Misrepresentation), and
the well-pleaded factual allegations supporting that conduct are now deemed established for
purposes of this prove-up.
30. I respectfully request that the Court award punitive damages in an amount the Court
finds just, reasonable, and constitutionally appropriate under State Farm Mut. Auto. Ins. Co. v.

WRIT OF EXECUTION OR SALE. Your rights and duties are indicated on the accompanying Notice of Levy (form EJ-150).  
 
WRIT OF POSSESSION OF PERSONAL PROPERTY. If the levying officer is not able to take custody of the property, the levying 
officer will demand that you turn over the property. If custody is not obtained following demand, the judgment may be enforced as a 
money judgment for the value of the property specified in the judgment or in a supplemental order.  
 
WRIT OF POSSESSION OF REAL PROPERTY. If the premises are not vacated within five days after the date of service on the  
occupant or, if service is by posting, within five days after service on you, the levying officer will remove the occupants from the real  
property and place the judgment creditor in possession of the property. Except for a mobile home, personal property remaining on the 
premises will be sold or otherwise disposed of in accordance with Code of Civil Procedure section 1174 unless you or the owner of the 
property pays the judgment creditor the reasonable cost of storage and takes possession of the personal property not later than 15 
days after the time the judgment creditor takes possession of the premises.  
 
EXCEPTION IF RENTAL HOUSING UNIT WAS FORECLOSED. If the residential property that you are renting was sold in a 
foreclosure, you have additional time before you must vacate the premises. If you have a lease for a fixed term, such as for a year, you 
may remain in the property until the term is up. If you have a periodic lease or tenancy, such as from month to month, you may remain 
in the property for 90 days after receiving a notice to quit. A blank Claim of Right to Possession and Notice of Hearing (form CP10) 
accompanies this writ. You may claim your right to remain on the property by filling it out and giving it to the sheriff or levying officer. 
 
EXCEPTION IF YOU WERE NOT SERVED WITH A FORM CALLED PREJUDGMENT CLAIM OF RIGHT TO POSSESSION. If you 
were not named in the judgment for possession and you occupied the premises on the date on which the unlawful detainer case was 
filed, you may object to the enforcement of the judgment against you. You must complete Claim of Right to Possession and Notice of 
Hearing (form CP10) and give it to the sheriff or levying officer. A blank form accompanies this writ. You have this right whether or not 
the property you are renting was sold in a foreclosure. 
 
JUDGMENTS FOR PERSONAL DEBT. If you are the judgment debtor identified in item 4 on this form, and if item 21 on this form says 
the judgment is for personal debt, the judgment creditor is required to verify your address before asking the levying officer to enforce 
this Writ of Execution. The judgment creditor must give the levying officer a completed copy of Declaration of Address Verification 
(form WG-015/EJ-135) and must file completed form WG-015/EJ-135 with the court within 10 business days of giving a copy of the 
form to the levying officer. If the judgment creditor doesn't take these steps, you can ask the court to stay any wage garnishment order, 
bank account levy, or other levy related to this Writ of Execution. You can use Application for Stay of Levy or Garnishment (form 
WG-017/EJ-137) to ask the court to stay the levy or garnishment until the address verification has been completed.

2. This Declaration is submitted together with the following companion documents
constituting my prove-up package as to Alpine: (a) Plaintiff's Request for Entry of Default and
Court Judgment (Form CIV-100); (b) this Declaration; and (c) the exhibits attached hereto, which
are the same documentary exhibits previously submitted in support of the default judgment
prove-up against co-defendant Diamond Truck Sales, Inc. ("Diamond"), attached again here so
that this filing is complete and self-contained as to Alpine.
II. PROCEDURAL POSTURE
3. The operative pleading in this action is the First Amended Complaint ("FAC"), which
names Alpine as a defendant on the theory that Alpine is Diamond's successor in interest, mere
continuation, de facto merger, and/or alter ego, and/or a participant in a fraudulent transfer under
the Uniform Voidable Transactions Act (Civ. Code section 3439 et seq.).
4. Alpine was personally served with the Amended Summons, the First Amended
Complaint, and the Notice of Case Assignment and Notice of Hearing on July 1, 2026, at 9:00
a.m., by delivery to Mustaqem Usmani, Manager, at 1201 S Soderquist Road, Turlock, California
95380, by San Joaquin County Sheriff's Deputy T. Caldwell, under Code of Civil Procedure
section 416.10. Proof of Service (Form POS-010, Levying Officer File No. 2026002577) was
signed July 2, 2026 by the Sheriff's Authorized Agent and is on file with this Court.

5. Alpine's deadline to respond to the FAC expired thirty (30) days after service, on July
31, 2026. Alpine filed no responsive pleading, demurrer, or other appearance, and no
meet-and-confer contact was received from Alpine at any time before or after that deadline. I
have submitted a Request for Entry of Default (Form CIV-100) against Alpine, and the Court has
entered, or will shortly enter, Alpine's default as reflected in the Court's file.
6. Because Alpine has defaulted, the well-pleaded factual allegations of the FAC
concerning Alpine's liability are deemed admitted. (Steven M. Garber & Assocs. v. Eskandarian
(2007) 150 Cal.App.4th 813, 823; Kim v. Westmoore Partners, Inc. (2011) 201 Cal.App.4th 267,
281.) The well-pleaded allegations include, without limitation: that Diamond rebranded to Alpine
during the pendency of this action; that Alpine has operated from the same locations as Diamond,
including 1201 S Soderquist Road, Turlock, California, under the same Osmani family ownership
and management; and that Alpine is therefore liable for Diamond's obligations in this action as its
successor in interest, mere continuation, de facto merger, and/or alter ego, and/or by reason of a
fraudulent transfer of Diamond's business and assets to Alpine.
7. This Declaration addresses only the amount and proof of damages as against Alpine. I
have made no effort to relitigate liability, which is deemed established by the default, nor to
relitigate the underlying fraud and misrepresentation claims against Diamond, which were proved
up separately -- and on the same exhibits reattached hereto -- in the default judgment package
previously submitted as to Diamond.
III. SUCCESSOR LIABILITY IS DERIVATIVE, NOT ADDITIONAL
8. Alpine's liability in this action is derivative of Diamond's liability. Alpine is not sued
for independently committing fraud, misrepresentation, or breach of contract in the underlying
vehicle sale transaction; rather, Alpine is sued as the entity that has, by operation of the
successor-liability and alter-ego doctrines pleaded in the FAC, become answerable for the single

9. Accordingly, Plaintiff does NOT seek, and this Declaration does NOT request, an
additional or duplicative award of damages against Alpine on top of the judgment sought against
Diamond. Plaintiff instead requests that judgment be entered against Alpine in the same total
amount requested against Diamond, on a joint and several basis, so that Plaintiff may recover the
single judgment sum from either or both defendants, without any double recovery. This is
consistent with the [Proposed] Judgment (Form JUD-100) already on file in this action, which at
item 8 expressly provides that "Alpine Truck Sales, Inc. is jointly and severally liable with
Diamond Truck Sales, Inc. as Diamond's successor, mere continuation, alter ego, and/or
fraudulent transference."
IV. DAMAGES (SAME SUM AS THE DIAMOND JUDGMENT)
10. The itemized calculation of damages is set forth in full in the Declaration in Support
of Request for Default Judgment previously filed against Diamond, and in Attachment 4b to
Plaintiff's Case Management Statement (Form CM-110) filed July 20, 2026, both of which are
incorporated herein by reference. The supporting documentary exhibits (Exhibits 1 through 10)
are attached to this Declaration for completeness. In summary: documented out-of-pocket losses
of $20,218.65; additional sworn, undocumented out-of-pocket losses of $5,750.00; conservatively
calculated lost commercial income of $23,400.00 (18 weeks x $1,300/week); and prejudgment
interest under Civil Code section 3287(a) (7%, approximately 3.04 years) of $4,302.55 -- for a
compensatory subtotal of $53,671.20.
11. Plaintiff additionally requests punitive damages of $25,000.00 under Civil Code
section 3294, based on the well-pleaded and, as to Diamond, now-admitted allegations that
Diamond's concealment of the DEF/SCR emissions defect was intentional, malicious, fraudulent,

Case No.: STK-CV-UF-2026-0001094
Brief Statement of the Case (CM-110, Item 4b):
On or about April 4, 2023, Plaintiff Brendan Ngwa Nforbi purchased a 2014 Volvo VNL diesel
semi-truck, VIN 4V4NC9EH6EN142206, from Defendant Diamond Truck Sales, Inc. for a total
price of $27,092.75, including a deposit of $12,345.10. Diamond knowingly concealed a material
defect in the truck's Diesel Exhaust Fluid (DEF) and Selective Catalytic Reduction (SCR)
emissions systems, rendering the truck non-compliant with California emissions law and unfit
for the lawful commercial highway operation for which it was purchased.
Shortly after purchase, the truck experienced engine derate (limp mode), emitted excessive
black smoke, and lost the ability to exceed approximately 35 mph, rendering it commercially
useless. The defect was pre-existing and known to Diamond through the prior owner's disclosure.
Alpine Truck Sales, Inc. is sued as Diamond's successor in interest, mere continuation, de facto
merger, alter ego, and/or as a participant in a fraudulent transfer under the Uniform Voidable
Transactions Act (Civ. Code 3439 et seq.). Diamond rebranded to Alpine during the pendency
of this action, operating from the same locations with the same Osmani family ownership.
Damages sought (per Declaration in Support of Default Judgment):
  Documented out-of-pocket losses:
    Deposit paid (Retail Buyer's Order):                    $12,345.10
    GAP Addendum enrollment:                                 $1,895.00
    CA DMV fees (billed; outstanding; penalties accruing):   $3,442.00
    Brannon Tire (emergency tire/road service):              $1,197.34
    Mobile Will's Truck/Auto Repair Shop:                      $740.00
    Golden Empire Towing, Inc.:                                $562.50
    Western Truck Center (lamp/parts):                          $36.71
    Subtotal documented:                                    $20,218.65
  Additional out-of-pocket (sworn testimony; no receipt):
    Commercial Towing (CVC 22852 storage release):             $750.00
    Almaraz Diesel (DEF/SCR diagnostic and repair):          $5,000.00
    Subtotal undocumented:                                   $5,750.00
  Lost commercial income (18 wks x $1,300/wk, conservative): $23,400.00
  Prejudgment interest (Civ. Code 3287(a), 7%, ~3.04 yrs):   $4,302.55
  SUBTOTAL COMPENSATORY:                                    $53,671.20
  Punitive damages (Civ. Code 3294):                        $25,000.00
  Costs of suit (per MC-010):                           per Memorandum
  TOTAL MONETARY JUDGMENT REQUESTED:      not less than $78,671.20
                                                          plus costs
Equitable relief sought: Rescission of the purchase transaction pursuant to Civil Code
sections 1689 and 1691; restitution of all monies paid; declaratory relief regarding the
enforceability of sale document provisions and Alpine's liability for Diamond's obligations;
injunctive relief under Bus. & Prof. Code 17200.

VII.  RESCISSION, RESTITUTION, AND DECLARATORY RELIEF
22. I gave notice of rescission within the FAC itself, as permitted by Civil Code sections
1691 and 1693. The truck has been irrecoverably damaged by the underlying defect and the
storage process. Restoration of the truck to its original condition is impossible and is therefore
excused under Civil Code section 1693, and this Court is authorized to adjust the equities
between the parties under that statute.
23. The $14,747.65 financed balance was originated through Dakota Financial LLC,
which is not a party to this action. I do not seek in this Declaration a money judgment in the
amount of the financed balance itself, because that obligation is between me and a non-party
lender and recovering it from Diamond would risk a double recovery if I later resolve the
financing separately.
24. I reserve the right, after entry of judgment, to seek a separate determination of any
indemnification or further restitution remedy as to the financed balance if and as appropriate
under Civil Code section 1693 and the Court's continuing equitable jurisdiction over the
rescission count.

Plaintiff Brendan Ngwa Nforbi ("Plaintiff") alleges as follows against Defendants
Diamond Truck Sales, Inc. ("Diamond"), Alpine Truck Sales, Inc. ("Alpine") (sued individually
and as the successor in interest, mere continuation, and/or alter ego of Diamond), and Does 1
through 20 (collectively, Defendants"):
Page 1
FIRST AMENDED COMPLAINT -- NGWA NFORBI v. DIAMOND/ALPINE TRUCK SALES

I. INTRODUCTION
1. This action arises from Diamond's knowing sale to Plaintiff of a 2014 Volvo VNL
commercial dicsel semi-truck (the "Truck") that Diamond knew, or had been specifically
informed by the prior owner, suffered from a material defect in its Diesel Exhaust Fluid ("DEF")
and Selective Catalytic Reduction ("SCR") emissions systems, rendering the Truck
non-compliant with California emissions law and unfit and unsafe for the lawful highway
operation for which it was sold.
2. Diamond is a sophisticated, multi-state commercial truck dealer with operations in
California, South Carolina, and Texas. Diamond is a licensed California vehicle dealer subject to
the California Vehicle Code, the Health and Safety Code, the regulations of the California Air
Resources Board ("CARB"), and the duty to disclose material defects affecting fitness, safety,
and regulatory compliance to its retail customers.
3. During the pendency of this action, and after Plaintiff caused the original Summons and
Complaint to be tendered to the Stanislaus County Sheriff for personal service on Diamond's
previously-designated agent for service of process, Plaintiff discovered that Diamond is
undergoing or has undergone a corporate rebranding to "Alpine Truck Sales, Inc.," with a
different person now publicly identified as the agent for service of process. Alpine continues
Diamond's identical commercial-truck-sales business from the identical four physical locations
historically associated with Diamond, with substantially the same family ownership, the same
management, and the same telephone, web, and contact infrastructure. As alleged below, Alpine
is liable on each cause of action herein on independent theories of (a) name change of the same
corporate entity, (b) successor liability by merc continuation and/or de facto merger, (c) express
or implied assumption of liabilities, (d) alter ego, and (e) fraudulent transfer designed to insulate
Diamond's assets from this and similar claims.
Page 2
FIRST AMENDED COMPLAINT -- NGWA NFORBI v. DIAMOND/ALPINE TRUCK SALES

4, Plaintiff, by contrast, is an individual commercial driver who relied entirely on
Diamond's superior position, regulatory licensure, and statutory and common-law duties of
disclosure when he purchased the Truck for use in his commercial freight operations centered in
California. Plaintiff would not have purchased the Truck -- and would not have paid the price he
paid, on the terms he accepted -- had Diamond disclosed the defect, the prior owner's pre-sale
notice to Diamond, the regulatory non-compliance, or the enforcement-agency status alleged
below.
5. Within a short time after purchase, while Plaintiff was operating the Truck under a
Lease-On Owner Operator Agreement on a commercial route, the Truck experienced exactly the
failure mode characteristic of the concealed defect: it entered engine derate ("limp mode"),
emitted excessive black smoke, and lost the ability to exceed approximately 35 miles per hour,
rendering it commercially useless and unsafe for highway operation. Plaintiff has suffered tens of
thousands of dollars in direct out-of-pocket losses and continues to suffer mounting consequential
losses including lost commercial freight income.
6. Plaintiff seeks rescission of the transaction, restitution of all consideration paid,
compensatory and consequential damages, punitive damages, restitution and injunctive relief
under the Unfair Competition Law, declaratory relief, costs, and prejudgment interest, jointly and
severally against Diamond and Alpine.
II. PARTIES
7. Plaintiff Brendan Ngwa Nforbi is, and at all times relevant hereto was, an individual
residing in Stockton, San Joaquin County, California.
8. Defendant Diamond Truck Sales, Inc. ("Diamond") is, and at all times relevant hereto
Page 3
FIRST AMENDED COMPLAINT NGWA NFORBI v. DIAMOND/ALPINE TRUCK SALES

was, a California corporation engaged in the business of selling commercial trucks, with locations
including 480 Peachoid Road, Gaffney, South Carolina 29341; 1201 South Soderquist Road,
Turlock, California 95380; 7156 Goldenstate Highway, Bakersfield, California 93308; and 5201
Bridge Street, Fort Worth, Texas 76103. Diamond is and was at all relevant times a licensed
California motor vehicle dealer subject to the California Vchicle Code, the California Health and
Safety Code, and the regulations of CARB.
9. Defendant Alpine Truck Sales, Inc. ("Alpine") is, on information and belief, a
California corporation engaged in the business of selling commercial trucks. Alpine operates fro
the same four physical locations historically associated with Diamond -- Turlock, Bakersfield,
Fort Worth, and Gaffney -- and continues Diamond's identical commercial-truck-sales business
with substantially the same management, ownership, employees, telephone numbers, customer
goodwill, and online presence. On information and belief, Alpine's currently designated agent for
service of process is Sheran Osmani, a member of the same Osmani family that controls
Diamond.
10. Liability of Alpine -- alternative theories. Plaintiff is informed and believes, and on
that basis alleges, that Alpine is liable for each and every claim asserted herein against Diamond,
on each of the following independent theories, pleaded in the alternative:
(a) Same entity / name change. Diamond Truck Sales, Inc. and Alpine Truck
Sales, Inc. are one and the same California corporate entity, with the entity having
amended its articles of incorporation or otherwise changed its name from "Diamond Truck
Sales, Inc." to "Alpine Truck Sales, Inc." Pursuant to Corporations Code sections 207 and
900 et seq., a corporate name change does not extinguish the corporation's pre-existing
(b) Mere continuation. Alpine is a "mere continuation" of Diamond, in that
Page 4
FIRST AMENDED COMPLAINT NGWA NFORBI v. DIAMOND/ALPINE TRUCK SALES

Alpine continues Diamond's identical business operations from the identical four physical
locations, with substantially the same ownership, management, employees, customers,
inventory, telephone numbers, and goodwill, and with no apparent payment of fair,
arms-length consideration in connection with any asset transfer (See Ray v. Alad Corp.
(1977) 19 Cal.3d 22, 28; Cleveland v. Johnson (2012) 209 Cal.App.4th 1315, 1326-1334);
(c) De facto merger. The transition from Diamond to Alpine constituted a de facto
merger, in that there was a continuity of ownership, management, personnel, and business
operations; an assumption by Alpine of the liabilities ordinarily necessary for the
uninterrupted continuation of normal business operations; a cessation of ordinary business
operations by Diamond; and a continuation of Diamond's business by Alpine (see Marks
v. Minnesota Mining & Mfg. Co. (1986) 187 Cal.App.3d 1429, 1436);
(d) Express or implied assumption. Alpine has expressly or impliedly assumed
Diamond's liabilities, including by holding itself out to Diamond's customers, the public,
regulators, and online platforms as the continuation of Diamond at the same locations and
under the continuing direction of the same controlling family;

INTRODUCTION
1. Plaintiff and Petitioner BRENDAN NGEHSI NEWANFORBI ("Plaintiff") brings this
action to challenge a systemic pattern and practice by the California Department of Corrections
and Rehabilitation ("CDCR") of imposing and enforcing parole conditions that lack the
constitutionally required nexus to a parolee's commitment offense—and then leveraging those
facially invalid conditions to manufacture detention without probable cause, due process, or
judicial oversight.

2. This action arises from—and seeks to prevent the recurrence of—a five-day unlawful
detention imposed on Plaintiff on or about November 1-6, 2024, when Defendant GLENN
URREA placed a parole hold on Plaintiff at the precise moment Plaintiff was otherwise eligible
for release from custody on an unrelated DUI booking. The hold was predicated on a purported
violation of Special Condition No. 063, a categorical "Halloween curfew" imposed without any
individualized nexus to Plaintiff's commitment offense—which involved an adult victim and bore
no connection whatsoever to Halloween, minors, or holiday-related conduct.
3. The unconstitutionality of CDCR's practice has been clearly established for decades. 
People v. Lent (1975) 15 Cal.3d 481 requires every parole condition to bear a rational nexus to
the offender's crime or future criminality. In re Ricardo P. (2019) 7 Cal.5th 1113 reaffirmed and
tightened that requirement. Yet CDCR continues to impose Special Condition No. 063 on PC §
290 registrants categorically, without individualized assessment, and to enforce it through
statewide "Operation Boo" detention sweeps. Plaintiff's detention was not an isolated clerical
error—it was the foreseeable product of policy.
4. Plaintiff remains on parole supervision into 2026 and beyond. Special Condition No.
063 has not been removed from his Conditions of Parole. Defendants' "Operation Boo" is an
annual enforcement event. Absent declaratory and injunctive relief, Plaintiff faces a concrete and
ongoing risk of repeated arbitrary detention every Halloween season.
5. Plaintiff seeks: (a) a writ of mandate compelling CDCR to remove Special Condition
No. 063 from Plaintiff's Conditions of Parole or, in the alternative, to conduct and document an
individualized nexus determination; (b) declaratory relief that Defendants' conduct violated the
California Constitution and California statutory law; (c) prospective injunctive relief requiring
CDCR to implement constitutionally adequate procedures governing the imposition and
enforcement of special parole conditions and parole holds; (d) damages under the Tom Bane Civil
Rights Act and California common law for the unlawful detention; and (e) attorney's fees, costs,

against Plaintiff in San Joaquin County, where Plaintiff resides and is under active parole
supervision. Plaintiff remains subject to "Operation Boo" enforcement in San Joaquin County
each year, and the prospective harm and ongoing violation of his constitutional rights are centered
in San Joaquin County. The continuing imposition and enforcement of Special Condition No. 063
by CDCR personnel supervising Plaintiff in San Joaquin County constitutes a substantial part of
the wrongful conduct and the prospective harm to which the requested writ, declaratory, and
injunctive relief is directed. Additionally, venue is proper in Sacramento County under Code of

BRENDAN NGEHSI NEWANFORBI ot
1455 Cat Tail Drive SUPERIOR COURT San Joa
Stockton, CA 95204 TSAN JOAQUIR
Plaintiff, In Pro Per STEPHANIE BOHRER, CLERK
COUNTY OF SAN JOAQUIN
BRENDAN NGEHSI NEWANFORBI,
Plaintiff,
v. COMPLAINT FOR DAMAGES
CALIFORNIA DEPARTMENT OF (Unlimited Civil Case)
CORRECTIONS AND REHABILITATION; )
KEELY DODD, in her individual capacity; 1. Negligence
GARY NOGUCHTI, in his individual capacity;
2. False Imprisonment
3. Intentional Infliction of
JOSEELYN ROJO, in her individual capacity;
Emotional Distress
and DOES 1 through 20, inclusive,
4. Brcach of Mandatory Duty
Defendants.
(Gov. Code Scc. 815.6)
Amount Demanded Exceeds $25,000
Bench Trial Elected
INTRODUCTION
1. Plaintiff BRENDAN NGEHSI NEWANFORBI brings this action for money damages
against Defendants the CALIFORNIA DEPARTMENT OF CORRECTIONS AND
REHABILITATION ("CDCR"), KEELY DODD, GARY NOGUCHI, JOSEELYN ROJO, and
DOES | through 20. This is a civil action at law for damages arising from the affirmative
misconduct of state actors who, having voluntarily undertaken to adjudicate Plaintiff's parole
status, executed that adjudication through a facially void instrument: a CDCR Form 1502-DR
Discharge Review Report that identifies a different parolee ("Eagan") by name, invokes a
fabricated "6.5-year" eligibility rule found in no statute or regulation, was prepared on an obsolete
Page 1
COMPLAINT FOR DAMAGES -- NEWANFORBI v. CDCR ET AL.

mandatory procedural safeguard, and was never served on Plaintiff.
2. This action does not seek Plaintiff's discharge from parole, an order compelling any
future parole decision, or any adjudication of the length of Plaintiff's parole term. Plaintiff
expressly docs not ask this Court to declare that he was entitled to carly discharge. Plaintiff secks
only retrospective and compensatory relief-money damages-for the discrete tortious acts of
individual state employees who exercised custodial power over him through an instrument that
was void on its face and that bore the name of another human being. These are remedies that lie
exclusively in a civil action at law and are categorically unavailable through a petition for writ of
habeas corpus.
3. The distinction is dispositive. A companion proceeding, Newanforbi v. Macomber
(Sacramento Super. Ct. No. 26WM000028), sought prospective relief-an order setting aside the
discharge determination and compelling an individualized review-through a petition for writ of
mandate. By tentative ruling dated May 29, 2026, the court held that such custody-directed,
prospective relief belongs in habeas corpus and that, because Penal Code section 3000(b)(2)(B)
imposes a ten-year parole term, CDCR had no duty under Penal Code section 3008 to conduct an
early individualized review. This complaint is fundamentally different in kind. It does not seek
release, does not seek a future review, and does not depend on any duty to discharge. It seeks
damages for completed torts. Habeas corpus cannot award lost wages, compliance costs,
emotional-distress damages, or punitive damages; only this civil action can.
4. Critically, even a court persuaded that Plaintiff must serve a ten-year term cannot
thereby license the affirmative wrongs alleged here. The lawfulness of Plaintiffs underlying
parole term and the lawfulness of the particular November 2025 instrument used to administer it
arc two separate questions. A state may have authority to supervise a person and still incur
liability when its agents exercise that authority through a fabricated, misidentified, and unserved
decree. The Macomber court itself found it "unclear why CDCR appeared to undertake parole
Page 2
COMPLAINT FOR DAMAGES -- NEWANFOREBI v. DODD ET AL.

discharge review" at all and noted that CDCR "refuse[d] to provide any explanation for this
course of conduct." Having elected to undertake that review, Defendants assumed a ministerial
duty to execute it lawfully. They did not.
5. As a direct and proximate result of Defendants' conduct, Plaintiff has suffered and
continues to suffer documented economic losses, out-of-pocket compliance costs, severe
emotional distress, and reputational harm. Plaintiff seeks compensatory damages, and punitive
damages against the individual Defendants whose willful, oppressive, and malicious conduct
warrants exemplary relief. Punitive damages are not sought against CDCR. (Gov. Code Sec. 818.)
PARTIES
6. Plaintiff BRENDAN NGEHSI NEWANFORBI is a natural person residing in
Stockton, San Joaquin County, California. He holds a valid Class A Commercial Driver's License
("CDL") and possesses the training and qualifications to earn approximately $72,000 per year as
journeyman CDL truck driver. He is presently supervised by CDCR's Division of Adult Parole
Operations ("DAPO"), Stockton 2 GPS Parole Unit, Region N.
7. Defendant KEELY DODD (Badge #6462) is a Parole Administrator employed by
CDCR/DAPO, On information and belief, Dodd's principal office and duty station are at DAPO
Northern Region Headquarters in Sacramento County. On November 19, 2025, Dodd was the
final approving official whose electronic signature converted a facially defective field
recommendation into an operative administrative decree. The report she approved applied
mutually exclusive parole-term frameworks, relied on a fabricated 6.5-year supervision rule,
identified a different parolee by name ("Eagan"), omitted all required good-cause and
Containment Tcam Meeting ("CTM") documentation, used an obsolete review form, and
reflected no service on Plaintiff. Dodd possessed authority to reject, correct, or remand the report
and declined to exercise it, instead recording the comment, "Concur with the Unit Supervisor,
Page 3
COMPLAINT FOR DAMAGES -- NEWANFOREBI v. DODD ET AL.

continued parole supervision is warranted and recommended at this time." As the final approving
official, Dodd had an independent duty to review the recommendation before adopting it, and
could not discharge that duty by reflexively deferring to subordinates. The defects were facial and
obvious; no reasonable administrator in Dodd's position could have relied on the recommendation
as a basis for action without first correcting the misidentification, the fabricated eligibility rule,
and the use of a superseded form. Dodd is sued individually pursuant to Government Code
section 820(a).
8. The CDCR Form 1502-DR recommendation was authored and electronically signed on
November 14, 2025 by CDCR/DAPO parole agent Long Moua (Badge #7472). Moua is not
named as a defendant in this action; his conduct is alleged as the act of a CDCR employee acting
within the course and scope of his employment, for which CDCR is responsible under
Government Code section 815.2(a), and as the factual predicate that the supervisory Defendants
thereafter ratified and finalized. In preparing the recommendation, Moua (a) inserted a fabricated
"10-year parole term" eligibility exclusion contradicting the report's own Case Type classification
of PC 3000(b)(5)(B); (b) fabricated a "6.5-year" minimum supervision requirement unsupported
by any enacted law; (c) applied a fabricated Policy 19-03 exclusion that does not exist in any
published version of that policy; (d) included internally contradictory characterizations; (e) failed
to aggregate the form's mandatory scoring criteria; (f) omitted all CTM documentation and Form
3043; and (g) used the obsolete CDCR Form 1502-DR (Rev. 01/22), The defects in Moua's
recommendation were not latent or buried; they were apparent on the face of the document to
anyone who read it. The recommendation named a different parolee, invoked an eligibility rule
that exists in no statute or regulation, and was prepared on a superseded form-errors that
required no investigation, no outside information, and no specialized judgment to detect. Any
reasonable reviewer exercising the most cursory examination would have identified them and
declined to adopt the recommendation without correction or remand.
9. Defendant GARY NOGUCHI (Badge #7284) is a Unit Supervisor employed by
Page 4
COMPLAINT FOR DAMAGES -- NEWANFORBI v. DODD ET AL.

CDCR/DAPO who reviewed and ratified the report, electronically signing it on November 19,
2025. Noguchi's written comments identify a different parolee-"Eagan"-by name, stating that
"Eagan has only completed approximately 4 years of the required 6.5 years of supervision."
Plaintiff is not Eagan. This misidentification appears in Noguchi's own comments and was his
own act; it is not something he merely failed to catch in a subordinate's work, and he therefore
cannot claim to have reasonably relied on the agent for it. Noguchi assessed Plaintiff as "Stable
6/LSCMI 5," a below-average risk level, yet endorsed retention; he simultaneously commended
Plaintiff for "maintaining compliance with parole supervision" while ratifying an adverse
recommendation. A supervisor reviewing a discharge recommendation has an independent duty
to verify the identity of the person whose liberty is at stake; the defects here were apparent on the
face of the document and foreclosed any reasonable reliance on the agent's work. Noguchi is sued
individually.
10. Defendant JOSEELYN ROJO is a Parole Agent employed by CDCR/DAPO who
assumed responsibility as Agent of Record on November 19, 2025. Rojo failed to serve the
finalized report on Plaintiff. The "Parolee Provided Copy (Date)" field on page 5 of the 1502-DR
is blank, and neither the "Mailed By" nor "Delivered By (Initials)" fields are completed. This
failure deprived Plaintiff of any opportunity to challenge the adverse decision and concealed its
existence from him. Rojo is sued individually.

of Plaintiff BRENDAN NGEHSI NEWANFORBI on California parole after a legally void

Stockton 2 GPS Parole Unit (Parole Agent Long Moua, Badge #7472, sued herein as a non-party
actor, not as a defendant) authored a CDCR Form 1502-DR Discharge Review Report that, on its
face, (a) applied mutually exclusive statutory parole-term frameworks, (b) relied on a
non-existent "6.5 years of supervision" eligibility rule, (c) applied a non-existent "10-year parole
term" exclusion attributed to an internal "Policy 19-03," (d) omitted every mandatory

3001(a)(2) has been articulated, documented, served on Plaintiff, or otherwise provided to him on
request. The statewide policies and practices that drove this result—including CDCR's continued
insistence that sex-offender-management-program participation must continue through the entire
parole term—were judicially condemned in In re Dwyer, San Mateo County Super. Ct. Case No.

before discharge from parole, as contemplated by Pen. Code section 3008(d)." Defendants
applied the pre-amendment framework to Plaintiff anyway.

SUMMARY OF CLAIMS
5. Scope of this action. Plaintiff does not in this action challenge the underlying 2018
judgment of conviction, his 2020 release to parole, or the existence of any original parole term.
This action challenges only (a) the November 2025 discharge-review determination reflected in
the CDCR Form 1502-DR attached as Exhibit A, (b) CDCR's continuing failure, since the
December 2, 2021 statutory one-year threshold, to perform the discharge-review procedures
mandated by Penal Code section 3001(a)(2) and Title 15, California Code of Regulations section
3574, and (c) the continuing effects of the unlawful retention on Plaintiff's liberty, economic
interests, and emotional well-being from November 19, 2025 forward. Within that scope, Plaintiff
alleges five causes of action:
(i) Breach of Mandatory Duty (Gov. Code §§ 815.2, 815.6) — CDCR failed to
perform the mandatory discharge-review procedures required by Penal Code sections
3000, 3001, and 3008, and by Title 15, California Code of Regulations section 3574,
before retaining Plaintiff after the December 2, 2021 one-year threshold and before the
November 19, 2025 denial of discharge. CDCR also bears vicarious liability under
Government Code section 815.2(a) for the acts and omissions of its supervisory
employees and of non-party Parole Agent Long Moua, the authoring agent;
(ii) False Imprisonment — the named individual Defendants caused and are
causing Plaintiff's continued custodial restraint without lawful privilege, by ratifying and
approving a review that applied fabricated eligibility rules, misidentified Plaintiff by
another parolee's name, omitted mandatory findings and documentation, and failed to
serve the decision on him;

20. Each cause of action is timely:

endures. (See Watts v. Johnson (2018) 27 Cal.App.5th 734, 744 [continuing tort;

November 19, 2025 onward is separately actionable.

years, subject to the same continuing-accrual analysis.

STATUTORY AND REGULATORY FRAMEWORK
21. Penal Code section 3001(a)(2) mandates discharge after one year. Penal Code
section 3001(a)(2) provides that a person required to register under Penal Code section 290 who
has been on parole continuously for one year "shall be discharged" unless the supervising agency
recommends retention and the Board of Parole Hearings, "for good cause, determines that the
person will be retained on parole." The Legislature's use of the word "shall" imposes a
mandatory, not discretionary, duty. (See Haggis v. City of Los Angeles (2000) 22 Cal.4th 490,
498–499 ["shall" is ordinarily mandatory for purposes of Government Code section 815.6].)
22. Penal Code section 3008(d) requires individualized treatment determinations.
Penal Code section 3008(d) authorizes sex-offender-management-program participation as part of
parole supervision but does not authorize retention for the entire term of parole as a matter of
blanket policy. In In re Dwyer, San Mateo Super. Ct. Case No. SC-080355A/HC-3020 (Mar. 20,
2023) (Exh. B), the court held that CDCR's policy of retaining all registrants in a management
program "for the entire term of parole, apparently without reference to the individualized
performance of each parolee," vitiates the Legislature's directive.
23. Title 15, California Code of Regulations section 3574 specifies the required
procedure and documentation. Section 3574, as amended effective April 17, 2025 and made
